She scored her first career brace in Nebraska’s NCAA First Round win over SDSU, helping the Huskers reach their program-best third trip to the Elite Eight and capture a Big Ten regular season title. She’s also proven herself internationally as a U20 World Cup Team Canada member.

The middle of the pitch just got stronger and Sadie is ready to make her mark in Ottawa.

The Waite is over Ottawa, our first new signing for 2026 is here. 

A four-season force at Nebraska with 73 appearances, 68 starts, and over 5,700 minutes on the pitch. Midfielder Sadie Waite contributed 8 goals and 10 assists, including a final season where she started every match and logged more than 1,500 minutes.

Brayden Bare and David Martinez provided the other two counting scores with 75s, while Jacob King is in a tie for sixth (+1) while playing as an individual.

Daniela Abonce registered her third top-15 finish of the season to lead UTSA to 12th place at the Collegiate Invitational at GCC.

Trojan family, join us in celebrating Black History Month ✌️

We begin by honoring the great Brice Taylor. Born without a left hand, Taylor overcame societal and physical barriers to become our first football All-American, and the first African-American football player at USC.

After his playing days, Taylor was named the Head Football Coach and Athletic Director at HBCU Southern University in Louisiana, where he led the Jaguars to their first undefeated season.

After that season, Taylor returned to Los Angeles and took the reins of Jefferson High School’s football program. In doing this, he became the first black head high school football coach in our city’s history.

Taylor went on to earn his doctorate degree and become a pastor at First African Methodist Episcopal Church in Los Angeles, the city he’d spend the rest of his life in.

Brice Taylor’s story is one of courage, strength, and leadership. He’s an example to all of us of what it means to be a true Trojan. ✌️

With so much excitement and confidence in this decision, I’m beyond excited to announce my commitment to the D1 volleyball program at the University of Central Florida to continue my academic and athletic career.

Francisco Solorza turned in his top finish of the season with a tie for 19th (72-80-75—227) and Sam Acharya tied for 25th (79-78-73—230) in his UTSA debut. Brayden Bare rounded out the lineup in 41st and Jacob King was 24th while playing as an individual.

The Adelaide Football Club is saddened by the passing of founding Crows Board member and Life Member Adrian Sutter.⁣
⁣
Sutter was one of the seven directors appointed by the SANFL to Adelaide’s Interim Board in October 1990 (pictured back row, second from right), tasked with establishing South Australia’s first AFL club for the 1991 season. ⁣
⁣
In these first four months he was also chairman of the Board’s administration sub-committee and secretary for the football committee. He was then elected to Adelaide’s inaugural board in February 1991 and served until the end of the 1996 season. ⁣
⁣
Our thoughts are with Adrian's family and friends at this time 🤍⁣

Recovering from not one but two hip surgeries took a mental toll on @carly.hendrickson. But with the help of family, friends, teammates, coaches and trainers, she was able to overcome the adversity of being on the sidelines and got herself back on the court.

Congrats on your CalHOPE Courage Award Carly!

Congrats to December CalHOPE Courage Award winner @carly.hendrickson!

Since November 2023 when she transferred from the University of Florida to UCLA, Carly has been tested both physically and emotionally. What began as a lingering hip issue during her sophomore season, eventually required surgery. That expected single procedure soon became two, forcing the Cincinnati, Ohio native to miss the entire 2024 season and spend more than a year away from competition. For an athlete whose identity was rooted in movement, teamwork, and competition, the extended absence from the court took a significant toll on her mental health.
 
Rather than withdrawing, Carly made a conscious choice to stay engaged. She attended every practice, remained a steady presence in the gym and locker room, and immersed herself in film study to deepen her understanding of the game. She found new ways to compete, challenging herself mentally, staying connected to her teammates, and redefining what contribution looked like when she couldn’t play.
 
“There were moments when it felt overwhelming being away from the game for so long. I missed competing, I missed the physical grind, and that was hard mentally,” said Carly. “What helped me was staying present every day, finding ways to challenge myself safely, staying around my teammates, and reminding myself that this process was about growth, not just getting back on the court.”
 
Cleared to return late in the year, Carly carried that growth into the 2025 season helping the Bruins to a 19-13 record including 128- in the conference and into the second round of the NCAA Tournament.  For the year she appeared in 101 sets in 29 matches as a rotational outside hitter.  She finished the year with 47 kills on 168 attempts, hitting .083, while adding 32 digs, 21 total blocks, placed second on the team with 25 service aces and 83.5 points.  Following her graduation from UCLA in December, Carly transferred to Vanderbilt University to continue her studies and complete her final year of eligibility for the Commodores.

Carly Hendrickson has received the @calhope_courage Award, recognizing California college athletes who have demonstrated exceptional resilience in the face of personal hardship.

Congratulations Carly!

Former UCLA men’s water polo player, Patrick Woepse, passed away on Thursday night, Oct. 10, at the age of 31. He died at a hospital surrounded by friends and family members in Newport Beach, Calif., after a 13-month battle with a rare form of aggressive stage 4 lung cancer (NUT carcinoma).

Woepse, who married UCLA women’s water polo standout and 2020 Olympic MVP, Maddie Musselman Woepse, was a five-year member of the Bruins’ team from 2012-16. He played for UCLA head coach Adam Wright and was an integral part of the 2014 and 2015 NCAA Championship teams that went on to set the UCLA, MPSF, and NCAA record for most consecutive victories at 57 (spanned 2014-16 seasons).

A GoFundMe has been set up to support Maddie and Patrick Woepse during this difficult time. Head to the link in our bio to support the family.

“All the hard work, sacrifices and the long way back from the pool to home, they are going to be worth it. It’s not the end of the world if you don’t perform the dive perfectly or win everything. A chip on the shoulder = proving to everyone else that you are good enough.
A crack on the shoulder = proving to themselves they're exactly who they say they are.

"THE best" is subjective.

Helping the players be THEIR best is the job of a coach.

Joshua “Josh” Ehrman
HS: Saline (‘13)
College: Purdue

- 13x MISCA All-State (‘10-13)
- 4x MHSAA D-1 Team champs (‘10-13)
- 13x NISCA All-American (‘10-13)
- 6x NAG Top 10 (‘10-12)
- 8x MHSAA D-1 champ (‘11-13)
- 3x MISCA Dream Team (‘11-13)
- State 15-16s 200m Breast record (‘11-21)
- MHSAA D-1 200 IM record (‘12-14)
- MHSAA All-Class 100 Breast record (‘12-15)
- MHSAA All-Class 400 Free Relay record (‘12)
- 2x MISCA D-1 Swimmer of the Year (‘12-13)
- WISC 15-18s 200 IM record (‘12-26)
- MHSAA All-Class 200 Medley Relay record (‘13-26)
- NISCA Public 200 Medley Relay record (‘13)
- MHSAA All-Class 200 IM record (‘13)
- Purdue school 800 Free Relay record (‘15-18)
- 2x Academic All-B1G (‘16-17)
- Big Ten Distinguished Scholar (‘17)

Ehrman combined with classmates David Boland (#8 in Series) and Adam Whitener (#219) to form one of the strongest trios in MHSAA history. They combined to win 33 state titles as Saline captured four consecutive Division I titles during their careers.

At the ‘12 D-1 meet Josh broke Dave Chernek’s 32-year old hold on the All-Class 100 Breast record, the longest-standing MHSAA mark in history. He held MHSAA records in four events during his career.

Ehrman joins Pioneer’s Sho Koba as the only two-time D-1 Swimmers of the Year since the MHSAA went to a division format in 2002-03. He is the third Saline alum and the second Purdue product recognized in the Series.

Today, February 4th, is National Girls and Women in Sport Day, and to honor #ngwsd, the RHBSSI is highlighting seven female student-athletes from all different Clemson sports! 

What does it mean to be a woman in sports?

“Being a woman in sports means being strong, resilient, and unstoppable,” Sade Gray, @clemsontrackxc, Marketing major 

“Being a woman in sports is all about representation and feeling confident in myself,” Bianca Martinez, @clemsontrackxc, @clemsonvb, Sociology major

“Being a woman in sports means having a big community of strong and inspirational women to look up to,” Madison Roush, @clemsontrackxc, Biomedical Engineering major

“Being a woman in sports means showing up with strength, discipline, and confidence in spaces that haven’t always made room for us,” Tatum Short @clemsonwsoccer, Psychology major 

“It means embracing the pressure that comes with higher expectations and learning how to carry myself with purpose both in competition and in everyday life,” Trinity Webb, @clemsongymnastics, Communications major

“It means overcoming challenges, proving my abilities, and staying confident in spaces where women are sometimes underestimated,” Shaunque Williams, @clemsontrackxc, Psychology major, RHBSSI Intern

“Being a woman in sports means pursuing passion and excellence while often overcoming inequality and stereotypes,” Oneka Wilson, @clemsontrackxc, Parks, Recreation and Tourism Management major

Click the link in our bio to learn more about their stories as women in sport!

We’re excited to feature our team doctor, Dr. Tenley (Palisin) Murphy, for our next alumni shoutout! ✨ We are so grateful to have a team doctor who understands our sport and shares our love for Clemson! 

Dr. Murphy’s journey is nothing short of remarkable:
🐅 Member of the inaugural Clemson Women’s Rowing team (Class of 2001)
🐅 University of South Carolina School of Medicine graduate (2005)
🐅 Completed a Sports Medicine fellowship following residency
🐅 Currently serves as Assistant Athletic Director of Sports Medicine at Clemson
🐅 One of the first women in sports medicine to serve as a Power 5 team physician 🔥
🐅 Has supported countless Clemson successes, including the Women’s Soccer College Cup, National Championships in Men’s Soccer, multiple ACC titles in Softball and Track

Dr. Murphy shared, “It’s been an incredible journey through sports medicine to provide care to our student-athletes, support them in their endeavors, and celebrate their successes.”

She is deeply grateful for the support of her husband, Dr. Brett Murphy, and their amazing daughter, Addison (13).

Thank you, Dr. Murphy, for all that you do for our team — and for continuing to inspire Clemson student-athletes on and off the water. 🧡💜🐅

Day 1 - Week 2:
Pause Plate Reverse Lunge
Upper emphasis day

Focus:
Intent

Considerations:
-Exploding from the bottom position.

-Using the pause (aka yielding isometric - muscles are working, but no movement in joint angle) at the bottom to remove the SSC (stretch-shortening cycle). 

-Doing so removes the stored elastic energy stored in the muscles & tendons, forcing us to produce force from a dead stop. 

-This also increases time under tension, which supports one of our early offseason goals of volume accumulation.

-Finally, this pause allows us to standardize a ROM or depth that we are looking to train out of. 

-Isometrics allow the athletes to spend more time in positions we intend to load, what these ranges should feel like, & helps me as a coach identify any compensations we may have (inability to stabilize, pelvis/hip shifting, flexion/extension/rotation of the torso, & so forth).

-Week 1 focus is technique (specifically the correct position/shape, followed by breathing). 

-Week 2 we then layer on the FOCUS of INTENT as an additional component of said technique. 

-As a coach, I only give the athlete ONE thing to focus on at a time. During week 1, if both position & breathing are already honed, intent is then instructed in real time. This is determined by our coaching eye & varies based on individual competency. 

-This is programmed on an upper body emphasis day, so for this week we used a 10# plate for each set as lower body loading is not a focus. Rehearsing high quality reps. 

-Holding the plate with both hands serves as a constraint to maintain an upright posture.

Eccentric Inverted Row
Upper emphasis day

Technique

-Our first set of this exercise pairing this semester. 
-Coaching 2 movements simultaneously. 
-Cadence makes life a lot easier when coaching larger groups as you can see everything at once. 
-Being week 1, the athletes are learning my cadence (only set I have with this view - I love how fast this group cleaned up their execution that session). 
-So as a coach I’m patient & expect a VERY brief adjustment period. This is a way to instill discipline as well.

Week 1 skill acquisition & setting standards:

Current early offseason training layout:

Day 1 Mon: UB1 (upper body emphasis)
Day 2 Tue: LB1 (lower body emphasis)
Day 3 Thur: UB2 (upper emphasis)
Day 4 Fri: LB2 (lower emphasis)

*Wed: Voluntary extra work or OFF*

We train full body every day, we jump every day, we play 🏐 every day, but the EMPHASIS changes each day. 

Is this layout the best way or only way you should train? Absolutely not. 

Shown are clips from Day 3 & 4 of our first week of offseason training. 

Day 3:
-Plate Squat at a cadenced tempo. 
(Future post coming focusing solely on coaching cadence). 
-Since this is an upper emphasis day we are minimally loading the lower body, but still being productive learning/rehearsing the squat pattern that we plan to load at higher intensities.

Day 4:
-Barbell Back Squat at the same cadenced tempo as the plate squats we did the day before. 
-Lower body emphasis day means we are programming higher intensity & volume of lower body work. This includes sprints/COD, jumps, & resistance training. 

Establishing execution standards:
Some of these athletes have never trained with me before. So:
-I’m learning how they move.
-They learn how I want them to execute.

Week 1 focus:
1) Range of motion (ROM)
2) Breathing

Everything you do (& think) is wiring your nervous system. This can be positive or negative. 

Just a few things I’m learning/making notes of:
-How each individual moves (EVERY practice/game/S&C session is a movement ASSESSMENT). 
-How does our new team interact with each other?
-How are the newcomers adjusting to their new environment?
-Which athletes are helping coach up their teammates?
-Who’s stepping up as leaders?
-Who’s encouraging/celebrating others?
-Who half asses what they do if I’m not standing near them?
-What do I need to do better? Did the session flow well based on how I set up the weight room & my exercise pairings? 
-How is our discipline when it comes to following instructions, cadence, etc? 

(Future post on coaching critique & post-session debriefs/reflections).

HONORARY MOUNTAINEER. What an honor. 🙏 

I had the privilege of speaking to the @wvubaseball team and being made an honorary West Virginia University Mountaineer. How badass is this jersey guys?!?!? 🔥

There’s something special about speaking to elite athletes. As someone who spent years on an elite team, I understand the mindset it takes to perform when everything is on the line.

Elite athletes get it:

✅ The discipline required for daily excellence
✅ The mental toughness to overcome setbacks
✅ The teamwork needed to achieve the impossible
✅ The leadership required in pressure moments

When I look at these players, I see the warrior spirit. 
The same commitment to being 1% better every day. The same refusal to accept mediocrity.
Speaking to sports teams isn’t just a job for me, it’s a passion. Whether it’s a college team fighting for a championship or a professional organization pushing for greatness, I understand what it takes to perform at the highest level.

The lessons from the battlefield translate directly to the playing field: Overcome adversity. Lead your team. Execute under pressure. Never quit.

These Mountaineers have what it takes. 
Now they have the mindset to match their talent.

BOOKING UPDATE: I’m only accepting a limited number of speaking engagements this year. If you know a company, sports team, or organization that needs an elite-level speaker who delivers real results, DM me for my booking information.

to training at the Belgian Top Sports School…

to joining Belgium’s senior Yellow Tigers training group…

Saar has been performing at the highest level her entire life.

WVU offers Saar the perfect environment to thrive:
✅ Big 12 competition with elite exposure
✅ A system built for high-impact outside hitters
✅ A coaching staff committed to international development
✅ Strong athletic facilities and support services
✅ A program ready to build around a top-tier European recruit

Staying connected to our roots keeps our program moving forward.

Lori Sherlock is an alumna that was on both the club and inaugural varsity team. Lori looks back at her time on the team fondly and remembers how crucial early support and personal connections were in making an impact on both her and the team.  This continues to this day through people like Lori who support and connect with both the university at large and the team. Lori is currently a Professor in Exercise Physiology, Aquatic Therapy Coordinator at WVU, and is always ready to step up for the team in any way she can.

Supporters like Lori have continued to stay connected to WVURowing as we’ve continued to grow, and we can’t wait to hear more of these stories and learn more about our roots as we bring back more alumni.

Ran the River to River Relay in southern IL today, which is 5 hours from home. How crazy is it to run into one of my past athletes! So good to see Angelo today!

XC Sectionals at Oregon. Not the greatest job by me on photos today. 

Ella got the chance for one more run today, closing out her senior year of competition. Darby unfortunately was sick and unable to run. For the last three XC seasons, Darby and Ella have been a part of it, and I’ll miss having them around!

We knew state qualifying was going to be an up hill battle for us , so our goals today were to have fun. That was it. I feel like that was accomplished. I’m proud of this team and love being their coach. 

#crosscountry #wearemarquette #maxctf

What happens when you make the bet to bleach your hair if your team qualifies for sectionals? Well… you follow through and hold up your end of the bet. 

I’ve been saying all along that we had what it takes to qualify, and the girls team advanced. They ran great on Saturday and earned one more week. And I earned the look of a mid life crisis. 😂

The number of looks and comments has been totally worth it. 

Special thanks to @amerydoe for the help with the process. Amery rocks!
#crosscountry #maxctf #wearemarquette #ihsasectionals

The Crusader guys cross country runners ended their seasons on a really strong note. 

Carson was a mid season addition to the team, wanting to get ready for basketball. Carson is a natural athlete, good at every sport he plays. He was good here too, and later admitted that XC was a lot harder than he was anticipating. For his final race of the season, he experienced the Seneca FFA course and all its challenges, and he handled them well, never looking like he was dying. 

And what to say about Joe. In his freshman season he accomplished so much. His first 3 mile race he ran a 25:48, and by the end of the season, he ran a 20:01, coming up just shy of breaking into the 19s, dropping 5:47 of time. 

He met his goal at regionals as well, wanting to drop over a minute on this course and run sub 21, and he did just that, finishing 20:58.9. 

Congrats to both guys on a heck of a season!!
#crosscountry #maxctf #wearemarquette #xcregionals

The Lady Cru advances! We get another week of the season and move on to the Oregon sectional. I’m super proud of how they battled today. 

I asked them to leave it all out on the course today, and they sure did (take a look at Maggie’s pic for proof) Shout out to Chloe, who wasn’t feeling her best but still gutted out a hard fought finish including a strong final kick. And Grace! She earns the belt this week as she stepped up and ran a great race, including completing a pass 2 feet from the finish line. That’s how you do it!
#crosscountry #maxctf #wearemarquette #xcregionals
Olivia was such a trooper - running an entire mile through town in a bear costume. 😂

Day before regionals and Halloween is approaching = COSTUME RUN through town!

Based on the number of honks, shouts from car windows and smiling faces, I think we brought some joy to all who saw us. 😃

#maxctf #crosscountry #wearemarquette

LWRB INVITE - pics 2. Joe and Carson are both learning a ton while gaining speed, with Joe just missing a new PR and Carson dropping 1:30 off his last race. 

Best finish of the day goes to Chloe, who found the next gear in her finishing sprint to outrun the opponent who led her the entire race until the last 400 meters. 

The BELT went to Keely, who set a new PR for the second race in a row!

The ladies team of Maggie, Morgan, Olivia, Keely, Chloe and Darby all worked hard and brought home a second place team finish, with Maggie and Morgan both inside the top ten! 

#marquettexctf #crosscountry #wearemarquette

LWRB INVITE - pics 1. This was a few days ago but the LWRB Invite in Roanoke is always a fun and challenging race filled with several PRs.

Congrats to Morgan, Keely, Chloe and Carson on their PRs for the day, while Darby and Joe ran their second fastest 3 mile race times ever. 

#marquettexctf #crosscountry #wearemarquette

LaSalle Co Meet Pics - batch 3!

Joe so far has been the lone runner for the Cru this season, but Carson asked if he could join in and here he is! 

Joe’s season has been filled with learning how to race and learning what he’s capable of, and it was on display again as he set another new PR, a 1:04 improvement!

Carson showed a lot of guts and determination as he learned what XC is like, and still finished :56 faster than what his hopeful finishing time was. 

Great job guys! 

And can we talk about how photogenic Joe’s hair is?

#crosscountry #wearemarquette #maxctf

LaSalle Co Meet Pics - batch 2. The ladies really brought it today, which is great to see as we enter into the second half of our season and head toward regionals. 

Congrats to our BELT winner, Chloe! Biggest PR of the day goes to her, with a 1:40 improvement! 

#wearemarquette #crosscountry #maxctf

LaSalle Co Meet pics - batch 1!

What a great day at Streator’s Eastwood golf course. 7 girls running today - with 2 PRs (Morgan and Chloe) and 5 Season’s best times. 

And the thumbs up pics means they’re having fun!

Way to make your coach happy!

Senior Spotlight: Jack Callan Edition💡

Favorite swimming memory?
Competing at the Olympic Trials in 2024, which was a goal I set all the way back in 2012 after watching the meet that year. Seeing all those years of hard work pay off was the most rewarding experience of my career.

What will you miss most from competing?
Being around my teammates every day because it has been my favorite part of the day-to-day process of this sport.

The biggest thing swim/dive has done for me?
Swimming has given me my closest friends in life. Whether it be teammates from club or college swimming, this sport has introduced me to many people that I couldn't imagine life without.
